text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Military ruler General Sani Abacha complains about United States' hostile attitude towards Nigeria to a visiting delegation from the Baptist Convention in the U.S.
- Court grants detained presidential claimant Moshood Abiola leave to compel provisional ruling council to appoint supreme court judges to handle all his pending court suits.
- Discount houses resist plans to raise their minimum capital base requirement above the current 100 million naira.
- Two oil firms, Mobil and Global Marine blaze the trail in utilising Nigeria's oil and gas export free zone, industry sources say.
- Nigeria has warned the Commonwealth of grave consequencs should it adopt measures inimical to the country's interest. A Commonwealth group is due to meet Nigerian dissidents in London on Thursday.
- Nigeria may lose as much as 40.48 billion naira on fuel importation because of subsidy which makes pump prices vastly lower than imported price of fuel.
- Finance minister Anthony Ani says government will not renege on its decision to liquidate 26 distressed banks.

- Government is reshaping its strategy on managing external debts by seeking to talk directly to individual creditor nations rather than through the Paris Club of Western creditor nations, according to official sources.
- Distressed banks need a total of 44 billion naira to recapitalise, says a report by the Nigerian Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC), which takes over when a bank goes under.
- Reported cases of fraud in the banks rose to 587 in 1996 from 127 in 1995, says the NDIC report.
- Irish oil firm, Tusker Resources, acquires interest in Nigerian offshore oil field.
